title: A discount declares its base and floor
question: Record gross/net selection, fractional-vs-percentage units, fixed reduction and zero clipping.

evidence.title: A discount chooses both a calculation base and a nonnegative floor
explanation: Fixed discounts subtract the same amount from net/gross and clamp each component at zero. Fractional discounts choose gross or net, quantize the discount amount, then apply the fixed discount.
Fractions/negative discounts are not bounded here; reducing both components independently can change effective tax. Tests cover zero clipping and base selection, not every sign/cap interaction.

evidence.title: Annual discount rounds a complementary share after full-period pricing
explanation: The annual-pricing example first multiplies monthly price by12, allocates a discount/complement pair, then subtracts the discount share.
The complement allocation determines where indivisible units go; this need not equal an independently rounded percentage multiplication.

The selected fixed discount ratio, source coefficient scale and Dinero allocation policy. A small indivisible discount can be affected by the larger complementary weight priority.
